missions.name: Mission San Diego de Alcalá
missions.status: Active Catholic parish and minor basilica (designated 1976 by Pope Paul VI); Diocese of San Diego.
missions.hours: Visitor Center open daily 9:00 am to 4:00 pm. Notice on the site: grounds and visitor center closed for a film production Fri Nov 20 (2026), 6 am to 6 pm.
missions.text: First of the 21 Alta California missions, founded July 16, 1769; known as the Mother of the Missions.
missions.more: In November 1775 Kumeyaay fighters burned the mission; Father Luis Jayme was killed and is called California's first Christian martyr. He is buried by the altar. Today's church is the fifth on the site: a 1931 rebuild that replicates the church dedicated November 12, 1813.
missions.visit: Inside: Church (basilica) and Father Jayme's tomb, 46-foot campanario with five bells (largest, Mater Dolorosa, 1,200 lb), Casa del Padre Serra room (CMF calls it the only original room to survive), Visitor center and gift shop.

missions.name: Carmel Mission
missions.name_es: Misión San Carlos Borromeo del Río Carmelo
missions.status: Active Catholic parish and minor basilica (1960, Pope John XXIII); Diocese of Monterey.
missions.hours: Closed Mon and Tue. Wed and Thu 10 am to 4 pm; Fri and Sat 10 am to 5 pm; Sun 11:30 am to 5 pm. Grounds close 15 minutes before the store. Closed New Year's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, Christmas and Dec 26.
missions.text: Serra's headquarters. He died on August 28, 1784, and is buried beneath the sanctuary floor.
missions.more: The stone church was completed in 1797. Its roof fell in 1852 and was replaced in 1884. Harry Downie restored the mission from 1931 for about 50 years; it is counted among the most authentically restored mission churches.
missions.visit: Inside: Basilica and Serra's burial place, Four museum galleries: Harry Downie Museum, Munras Family Heritage Museum, Jo Mora Chapel Gallery (1924 Serra cenotaph), Convento Museum with Serra's cell, Cemetery and grounds, Mission store.

missions.name: Mission San Antonio de Padua
missions.status: Catholic church, museum and retreat center of the Diocese of Monterey; surrounded by the Army's Fort Hunter Liggett.
missions.hours: Closed Mon and Tue. Wed to Sat 10 am to 4 pm; Sun 11:30 am to 4 pm. Posted closures: Nov 23 to 27, 2026; Dec 21 to 26 (except Dec 24 5 pm Mass); Dec 28, 2026 to Jan 2, 2027. Directions: US-101 exit 252, 26 miles on Jolon Road, then about 5.75 miles on Mission Road inside Fort Hunter Liggett.
missions.text: Third mission, founded by Serra on July 14, 1771; the site marked its 255th anniversary on July 14, 2026.
missions.more: Credited with the first fired red tile roof in Alta California (San Luis Obispo has a competing tile story). Its mission-era aqueduct and water system from the San Antonio River is described as the most complete in California.
missions.visit: Inside: Church (begun 1810, restored in the 20th century), Museum of Native American and mission-era archaeology, Water system ruins and grounds, Gift shop, retreat center, fiesta grounds.

missions.name: Mission San Gabriel
missions.founder: Fathers Pedro Benito Cambón and Ángel Fernández de la Somera, under Serra's authority (CMF credits Serra himself).
missions.people: Tongva / Gabrieleño (Gabrielino); the Kizh Nation prefers Kizh
missions.status: Catholic parish church of the Archdiocese of Los Angeles, run by the Claretian Missionaries since 1908; museum. Reopened July 1, 2023.
missions.hours: UNVERIFIED on the official site (sangabrielmissionchurch.org returned 403). CMF lists 9:00 am to 4:30 pm daily; closed New Year's, Easter, July 4, Thanksgiving, Christmas; closes noon Christmas Eve.
missions.text: Church completed 1805, designed by Father Antonio Cruzado with capped buttresses and tall narrow windows unlike any other mission; CMF ties the style to the cathedral of Córdoba.
missions.more: The December 8, 1812 earthquake toppled the original bell tower; the six-bell campanario replaced it. An arson fire on July 11, 2020 destroyed the church roof. The campus reopened July 1, 2023 with a new museum exhibit naming 7,054 Native people baptized 1771 to 1848.
missions.visit: Inside: Church, Museum (2023 exhibit 'Mission San Gabriel Arcángel, 1771-1900: Natives, Missionaries, and the Birth of Catholicism in Los Angeles', Wall of Names), Six-bell campanario, Cemetery and gardens.

missions.name: Mission San Luis Obispo
missions.name_es: Misión San Luis Obispo de Tolosa
missions.people: Northern Chumash (yak titʸu titʸu yak tiłhini); the mission-era language is called Obispeño
missions.status: Active Catholic parish (Old Mission Parish), Diocese of Monterey; museum.
missions.hours: Mission doors open every day of the year. Museum and gift shop Wed to Sun 11 am to 4:30 pm. Docent tours Mon to Fri 1:15 pm, Sat 2 pm, Sun 2:30 pm (extra tours April 1 to Labor Day).
missions.text: Site chosen after a 1772 bear hunt in the 'llano de los osos' (plain of the bears) fed hungry Monterey and Carmel.
missions.more: After a flaming arrow set roofs on fire in 1776, the padres began making fired roof tiles here. Only L-shaped mission church in California, with a second nave beside the altar.
missions.visit: Inside: Church (open every day), Museum and gift shop, Mission Plaza with grizzly bear statue, Docent tours.

missions.name: Mission Dolores
missions.founder: Father Francisco Palóu (with Father Pedro Benito Cambón), under Serra's authority; often credited to Serra.
missions.people: Ramaytush Ohlone (Yelamu were the San Francisco group); Coast Miwok and others were later brought here
missions.status: Active Catholic parish, Archdiocese of San Francisco. The adjacent Mission Dolores Basilica (completed 1918) was named a minor basilica in 1952 by Pope Pius XII.
missions.hours: Mon to Fri 10 am to 4 pm; Sat and Sun 10 am to 5 pm. Self-guided, no reservation needed; guided tours paused.
missions.text: The adobe chapel, completed in 1791 with about 36,000 adobe bricks made by Ohlone workers, is the oldest intact building in San Francisco.
missions.more: It survived the 1906 earthquake; the 1876 brick church next door did not and was replaced by today's basilica. The ceiling shows Ohlone designs painted in vegetable dyes.
missions.visit: Inside: Old Mission chapel, Mission Dolores Basilica, Museum and gift shop, Cemetery and gardens, including an Ohlone ethnobotanic garden and a rose garden.

missions.name: Mission San Juan Capistrano
missions.founder: Junípero Serra (1776; Wikipedia adds Gregorio Amúrrio); first attempt by Fermín Lasuén (1775)
missions.status: Mission compound is a museum and historic landmark; the Serra Chapel serves the mission parish. The adjacent modern Mission Basilica San Juan Capistrano became a minor basilica in 2000. Diocese of Orange.
missions.hours: Tue to Sun 9 am to 5 pm (admission sold until 4:45). Mon closed to general admission (appointments only). Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day; closed for the gala on Sept 18, 2026.
missions.text: The Serra Chapel (1782) is regarded as the oldest building in California still in use and the last standing church where Serra is known to have said Mass.
missions.more: The Great Stone Church, begun 1797 and finished 1806, collapsed in the December 8, 1812 earthquake during Mass on the feast of the Immaculate Conception; about 40 worshipers died (Wikipedia adds two boys ringing the bells). The return of the swallows is celebrated each year on St. Joseph's Day, March 19.
missions.visit: Inside: Serra Chapel with its gilded Baroque retablo, Great Stone Church ruins, Museum exhibits, Gardens.

missions.name: Mission Santa Clara
missions.name_es: Misión Santa Clara de Asís (first called Santa Clara de Thamien)
missions.founder: Father Tomás de la Peña (celebrated the first Mass), under Serra's authority; usually credited to Serra
missions.people: Tamien (Thamien) Ohlone; later also Bay Miwok and Yokuts
missions.status: Santa Clara University chapel (Jesuit) and parish church; the only mission the Franciscans handed to the Jesuits (1851).
missions.hours: Church open every day 7 am to 7 pm.
missions.text: First California mission named for a woman, St. Clare of Assisi.
missions.more: The present church (1928 to 1929) re-creates the 1825 church destroyed by fire in October 1926. In 1851 the Jesuits opened a college here that became Santa Clara University, the oldest university in California; it is the only mission on a university campus.
missions.visit: Inside: Mission church, Mission gardens on campus, Self-guided walking tour (PDF) and virtual tours.

missions.name: Mission Basilica San Buenaventura
missions.founder: Junípero Serra (the last mission he founded)
missions.status: Active Catholic parish, Archdiocese of Los Angeles; minor basilica by Pope Francis (decree documents dated June 9, 2020; proclaimed July 15, 2020).
missions.hours: Gift shop and museum daily 9 am to 4:30 pm; self-guided tour daily 9 am to 4 pm. Closed Easter, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Day. (The site's Visitors page still says 10 am to 5 pm.)
missions.text: Ninth mission and the last founded by Serra, on Easter Sunday, March 31, 1782.
missions.more: Church dedicated 1809; the 1812 earthquakes and sea wave sent friars and Chumash inland; an 1893 'modernization' painted over the art; restoration finished 1957. Two wooden bells in the museum are the only wooden bells known from the California missions.
missions.visit: Inside: Basilica church, Museum (wooden bells, Chumash and mission items), Garden and grotto, 30-minute video.

missions.name: Old Mission Santa Barbara
missions.status: Active parish church of the Archdiocese of Los Angeles where Franciscan friars have lived continuously since 1786; museum.
missions.hours: Self-guided tour and museum Mon to Sat 9:30 am to 5 pm; Sun 12:30 pm to 5 pm; last ticket 4 pm. Church and cemetery leave the tour Sat after 3:15 pm, Sun 9:30 am to 12:30 pm, and for weddings and funerals.
missions.text: The friars 'have lived continuously at Mission Santa Barbara since they founded' it in 1786 (mission homepage). CMF and Wikipedia pair it with San Luis Rey, but San Luis Rey had a gap until 1893.
missions.more: The December 21, 1812 earthquake destroyed the third church; the present stone church was built about 1815 to 1820 (CMF says 1812 to 1820). The twin towers were damaged in the June 29, 1925 earthquake; the facade and towers were taken down and rebuilt in their original form in 1950 to 1953.
missions.visit: Inside: Church, Historic cemetery and mausoleum, Nine-room museum, Gardens on 15 acres.

missions.name: La Purísima Mission
missions.name_es: Misión La Purísima Concepción de María Santísima
missions.status: La Purísima Mission State Historic Park, California State Parks. Not a church; with Sonoma one of two missions not governed by the Catholic Church.
missions.hours: Historic buildings 9 am to 4 pm; parking lot 9 am to 5 pm; visitor center Tue to Sun 10 am to 4 pm; trails 6 am to sunset. Closed New Year's Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas.
missions.text: Described by State Parks as the most completely restored mission in California.
missions.more: The Civilian Conservation Corps rebuilt it from ruins starting in 1934; it was dedicated on December 7, 1941, the day the US entered World War II. In the 1824 Chumash revolt, Chumash people held the mission for about a month.
missions.visit: Inside: Main church and Padre's chapel, Ten restored and furnished buildings (shops, quarters, blacksmith), Five-acre historic garden, Corrals with burros, horses, longhorn cattle, sheep, goats.

missions.name: Mission Santa Cruz
missions.name_es: Misión la Exaltación de la Santa Cruz
missions.status: Replica chapel (1931) belongs to Holy Cross Parish, Diocese of Monterey. The surviving adobe is Santa Cruz Mission State Historic Park.
missions.hours: State Historic Park adobe: Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Monday 10 am to 4 pm, as posted; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas. Replica chapel hours not posted; CMF lists the Galería Tue to Sat 10 am to 4 pm, Sun 10 am to 2 pm.
missions.text: The one surviving original building is an adobe (built 1822 to 1824) that housed Native families; State Parks says it is the only example of its kind still standing in California.
missions.more: The adobe church's front wall fell in the 1857 Fort Tejon earthquake; CMF also cites an 1845 quake that toppled the bell tower. Holy Cross Church (1889) stands over part of the old church. The 1931 replica chapel was based on an 1876 painting by Léon Trousset and is smaller than the original (CMF: one third the size).
missions.visit: Inside: Replica chapel (CMF: original paintings, statues, a chalice used by Serra), Holy Cross Church, State Historic Park adobe with Ohlone and Yokuts exhibits, Mission Galería (CMF).

missions.name: Mission Soledad
missions.name_es: Misión Nuestra Señora de la Soledad
missions.status: Chapel of Our Lady of Solitude parish, Diocese of Monterey; museum; not state funded, relies on donations.
missions.hours: Tue to Sun 10 am to 4 pm; closed Mondays and several holidays.
missions.text: Governor José Joaquín de Arrillaga died here on July 24, 1814 and was buried in the chapel.
missions.more: Salinas River floods hit in 1824, 1828 and 1832 (CMF: the 1828 flood destroyed the church, rebuilt 1832). After secularization it was sold for a reported $800 and left in ruins.
missions.visit: Inside: Rebuilt chapel, Museum in the convento wing (original mission bell, CMF), Unrestored adobe ruins of the quadrangle, Cemetery with Governor Arrillaga's grave marker.

missions.name: Mission San Jose
missions.people: Ohlone (Chochenyo speakers); later Bay Miwok, Yokuts, Patwin, Coast and Plains Miwok
missions.status: Catholic church of Saint Joseph Parish, Diocese of Oakland; museum.
missions.hours: Closed Mon and Tue. Wed to Fri 10 am to 3 pm; Sat and Sun 10 am to 4:30 pm. Closed Easter, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's. Guided tours second weekend of each month by reservation.
missions.text: The October 21, 1868 Hayward Fault earthquake shattered the adobe church.
missions.more: Today's church is a replica of the 1809 adobe church, built 1982 to 1985 and rededicated June 11, 1985. Father Narciso Durán trained a Native choir and a 30-piece orchestra famous across California.
missions.visit: Inside: Replica 1809 church, Museum in a surviving original adobe wing, Cemetery (entered through the museum), Grounds (free).

missions.name: Mission San Juan Bautista
missions.status: Active Catholic parish, Diocese of Monterey; faces the plaza of San Juan Bautista State Historic Park (a state park since 1933).
missions.hours: Gift shop, museum and garden Wed to Sun 9 am to 4 pm. Closed New Year's, Thanksgiving, Christmas and other holidays.
missions.text: The only three-aisle church among the missions; the side aisles were walled in after 1812 earthquake damage and reopened in 1975.
missions.more: Built beside the San Andreas Fault; the 1906 earthquake ruined the outer church walls. A preserved stretch of the old El Camino Real runs below the cemetery wall along the fault. Father Estevan Tapis taught a Native boys' choir with color-coded notation, earning the name Mission of Music.
missions.visit: Inside: Church (three aisles), Museum, Garden, Cemetery.

missions.name: Mission San Miguel
missions.status: Catholic parish church of the Diocese of Monterey; Franciscans returned in 1928 (Wikipedia). Whether friars still staff it today is UNVERIFIED.
missions.hours: UNVERIFIED on the official site (returned 403). CMF lists 9:30 am to 4:30 pm daily; phone 805-467-3256.
missions.text: Interior murals painted by Salinan artists under Esteban Munras in the 1820s have never been repainted.
missions.more: The church was built 1816 to 1818 after an 1806 fire destroyed the earlier one. Closed after the December 22, 2003 San Simeon earthquake; reopened in 2009 (September 29 per Wikipedia, October 2 per CMF).
missions.visit: Inside: Church with original murals, Original arcade, Museum and gift shop, Cemetery.

missions.name: Mission San Fernando
missions.name_es: Misión San Fernando Rey de España
missions.status: Archdiocese of Los Angeles; the church is a chapel of ease and the grounds a museum.
missions.hours: 9 am to 4:30 pm daily (CMF and the Archdiocese listing). No official mission website found; the Archdiocese links to the California Missions Resource Center page.
missions.text: The church was destroyed by the 1971 San Fernando earthquake and rebuilt by 1974.
missions.more: The convento, finished in 1822 after twelve years of work, has a 19-arch colonnade. Bob Hope (2003) and Dolores Hope (2011) are buried in the Bob Hope Memorial Gardens.
missions.visit: Inside: Rebuilt church, Convento and museum, Gardens and fountain, Replica winery.

missions.name: Mission San Luis Rey
missions.name_es: Misión San Luis Rey de Francia
missions.status: Parish, museum, cemetery and retreat center; a ministry of the Franciscan Friars, Province of Saint Barbara; Diocese of San Diego.
missions.hours: Museum daily 10 am to 4 pm; gift shop 10 am to 5 pm; church Mon to Sat 8 am to 4 pm, Sun 7 am to 4 pm; cemetery 7 am to 5 pm.
missions.text: Called the King of the Missions for its size; the mission calls itself the largest of California's missions, with 2,869 people in 1825 (CMF).
missions.more: The 1815 church is the only surviving mission church built in a cross shape, with a wooden dome and cupola. California's first pepper tree, from Peru, was planted here in 1830.
missions.visit: Inside: Historic church, Museum, Madonna Chapel, Cemetery (original 1798).

missions.name: Mission Santa Inés
missions.status: Catholic parish of the Archdiocese of Los Angeles, served by Capuchin Franciscan friars since 1924; museum.
missions.hours: Self-guided tours 9 am to 4:30 pm; gift shop 9 am to 5 pm. Gift shop and museum closed New Year's, Easter, July 4, Thanksgiving, Christmas.
missions.text: The December 21, 1812 earthquake destroyed most of the first church; the present church was dedicated July 4, 1817.
missions.more: The Chumash revolt of 1824 began here on February 21, 1824, after a soldier beat a young Chumash man. California's first college seminary opened here in 1844.
missions.visit: Inside: Church, Museum with vestments, art, manuscripts and bells, Mission garden and rose garden, Gift shop.

missions.name: Mission San Rafael
missions.status: Replica chapel (1949) of St. Raphael Parish, Archdiocese of San Francisco (parish since 1884).
missions.hours: Not posted online. Parish office 9 am to 5:30 pm, (415) 454-8141. CMF lists 11 am to 4 pm daily, call to confirm.
missions.text: Founded to care for sick Native people from foggy San Francisco, Alta California's first sanitarium; named for the archangel of healing.
missions.more: The ruins were completely removed by 1870, earning it the name 'most obliterated' of the missions. The replica chapel was built in 1949 near the original hospital site beside the 1919 parish church (CMF's text also says 1940).
missions.visit: Inside: Replica chapel, Small museum and gift shop (hours not posted), St. Raphael Church.

missions.name: Sonoma Mission
missions.people: Coast Miwok, Southern Pomo, Wappo and Patwin (Suisunes)
missions.status: Museum in Sonoma State Historic Park, California State Parks. Not a church.
missions.hours: Open daily 10 am to 5 pm; closed Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Day. Gift shop 10 am to 4:30 pm.
missions.text: The 21st, last and northernmost mission, and the only one founded after Mexico's independence.
missions.more: Governor Luis Argüello backed it partly to block Russian expansion from Fort Ross and Bodega Bay. The present adobe chapel was built in 1841 on Mariano Vallejo's orders, on the site of the first wooden chapel.
missions.visit: Inside: 1841 adobe chapel, Convento museum, Chris Jorgensen mission paintings, Sonoma Mission Indian Memorial.
